concerns.why: Standalone @astralyn/pi packaging, identity, update source, and disabled install telemetry.

paths.rewrite: The first-run gate compares against this distribution's package metadata, replacing upstream's official-distribution constants.

Repository source policy loads every grammar through static imports instead of upstream's deferred dynamic import.
Update checks read the npm registry, whose response replaces upstream's pi.dev payload fields.
The distribution ships a shrinkwrap, so the upstream npm-to-pi.dev migration notice is inapplicable and would replace the installed distribution.

concerns.why: The distribution adds configurable bundled extensions alongside upstream built-ins.

paths.rewrite: TaskSession owns result and usage persistence; TaskDelivery owns queued completion and tool-call receipts. Lifecycle pauses wrap upstream-shaped Body methods, and TasksContext.session exposes the narrow host bridge used by the management extension.
The task-usage ledger counts once per task, which turns upstream's accounting loop into a shared generator.
Footer totals read the shared accounted-usage ledger instead of summing session entries inline.
The base tool map routes bash and powershell through the managed definition while upstream keeps the process loop, so its export and import block splits across modules.

concerns.why: Extensions capture detached, stable model input and request settings without writing to the session.

Verify native fallback and HTML export as well as interactive states.

The interactive host constructs the native component and obtains its shell through the existing renderer resolver.
